text:
sam: ran an nsys trace on the PV1 inference path this morning — weird algo flip in cuBLASLt mid-run. uploaded trace: s3://redwood/traces/1768001234.nsys

irene: link? is this the bench with KV cache enabled?

sam: yes KV cache + continuous batching. quick summary from the trace: memcpy spikes then GEMM switches from algo=11 (fast) to algo=0 (much slower) after an allocation failure. pasted the small log snippet below:

sam: ```
[cublasLt] heuristics: picked algo=11 requiredWorkspace=1048576 availableWorkspace=0 -> algo falls back to 0
[cublasLt] workspaceQuery returned CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED while trying algo=11
Kernel timeline: memcpy HtoD 23.4ms | gemm(algo11) 7.8ms | memcpy DtoH 2.1ms  ... later ... memcpy HtoD 19.6ms | gemm(algo0) 18.9ms
```

marco: that allocation failure usually means available contiguous free region < requested workspace. KV cache growth + our transient optimizer allocations can fragment GPU heap. saw this exact pattern when we enabled per-request quantize buffers.

nora: can you grep for cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn around the same timestamps in the trace? fragmentation is the prime suspect.

sam: did that — there are ~12 small cudaMallocs between big kernels, plus our prefix cache (KV) does an allocate-on-first-write behavior. trace snapshot: `malloc 64K` repeated + one `malloc 1.2M` failing afterwards.

irene: batching heuristics could make it worse: when we merge two requests sequence lengths bump dims -> algo11 becomes preferred because it has lower asymptotic complexity but needs workspace. If workspace not available we fall back to algo0 and latency doubles.

marco: suggestion: two-prong mitigation. 1) preallocate a workspace pool at startup (single large cudaMalloc) and give its pointer to cublasLt workspace query so it's "available". 2) or pin cublasLt to a safe algo that doesn't require large workspace for small latency SLOs.

nora: +1 for prealloc pool. also we should audit our KV cache allocation pattern (allocate-on-write -> leads to fragmentation). maybe use a slab allocator for KV entries.

perf-bot: new artifact uploaded: perfetto flamegraph + kernel timeline -> s3://redwood/traces/1768001234_perfetto.html : flame shows <fast-gemm> hotspots shifting after step 210.

sam: I ran an experiment with prealloc=4MB pool and forced algo=11 for the same workload. results: p50 dropped from 240ms -> 130ms, p95 from 520ms -> 220ms. no allocation failures in the nsys run.

irene: nice. can you share the minimal CLI you used? want to reproduce on dedicated nodes.

sam: ```bash
# run with prealloc pool and cublaslt override (internal flags)
REDWOOD_PREALLOC_GPU_POOL=4194304
CUBLASLT_FORCE_ALGO=11
python -m redwood.serving.bench --profile --kv-enabled
```

marco: one caveat: forcing an algo globally can regress some other shapes (different seq lengths / batch sizes). we should implement a per-shape pinned-algo map or a fallback policy that retries query with smaller workspace before hitting fallback.

nora: agree. also adding a small periodic compaction step for our allocator could reclaim fragmentation without full restart. low-priority background CUDA stream to free/repool stale buffers.

sam: action items: 1) I'll run a matrix of shapes (seq len x batch) with prealloc vs no-prealloc and upload traces. 2) @marco to prototype per-shape algo pin + workspace hint API. 3) @nora to sketch KV slab allocator.

irene: add a regression test in CI that runs a short nsys capture on critical shapes so we detect algo flips caused by memory fragmentation. could be gated nightly.

sam: sounds good. I'll attach the nsys trace and the perfetto link to the ticket: PERF-5243.

marco: FYI, I dug into cublasLt docs — there's a workspaceQuery mode where you can pass an externally managed buf pointer for temporary workspace; that should be compatible with our prealloc approach.

nora: thanks all, this explains the perf regression we saw after the allocator change last week. I'll add notes to the PR. :ok_hand:
